title: the-loop-names-its-own-staleness-instead-of-benching-a-device
owner: CC owns the code and the proofs. Akien owns the one bound CC may not touch and it is named here so no build quietly reaches for it: the 5s liveness threshold is RULED, and widening it to make the DEAD flicker go away would be exactly the plaster the 2026-08-14 rule forbids
intention: When a probe cannot be loaded because THIS PROCESS is older than the code it is reading, the ground loop says that about ITSELF and does not bench the device — so the watch layer cannot be switched off by an ordinary rename.
why: BECAUSE IT ALREADY WAS, FOR 29 HOURS, AND NOTHING IN THE SYSTEM NOTICED. Fifteen devices carrying twenty-two probes — every WATCHME armed since 2026-08-13 15:35:43 — were skipped by the heartbeat for a defect that was never theirs. The lived symptom is not abstract: a build arms a watch, seals it, records it as PROVED, and the watch never fires once; the next mind reads a green record and a silent probe and has no way to tell that from a watch that fired and found nothing. Akien's standing frame, 2026-08-14: 'we keep on until this whole skills and mechanical workflow is solid' — and a watch layer a rename turns off is the least solid thing in it, because every WATCHME every future build arms lands in exactly the folder this defect darkens.
traces_to: Law 3 — nothing is known until measured. A benched device emits nothing, so every watch behind it was an unmeasured claim wearing a sealed record's clothes.
Law 9 — red is the default and green is earned. Twenty-two probes read as green-and-quiet for 29 hours while never running; quiet was taken for earned.
Law 10 — nothing in the system is immeasurable. Every input to the missing predicate (process start time, file mtimes, the module file behind a class) was free on disk the whole time.
Akien 2026-08-14 — 'we keep on until this whole skills and mechanical workflow is solid'.
I-shrinking-footprint-event-not-poll — the staleness predicate runs only on the failure path, which is empty in the healthy case.

falsifier.proves_green: THREE PIECES AND THE THIRD IS WHAT MAKES THE FIRST TWO MORE THAN A NICER MESSAGE. (1) DETECT: on a probe-load failure, the loop evaluates one predicate — is this process older than the code it is judging — from the process start time, the mtime of the files involved, and, for the identity case, the module file behind the loaded class compared against the module file behind the loop's own. Both observed faces fall out of it: the isinstance mismatch where two module identities carry one class name, and the ImportError where a symbol exists on disk but not in the loaded module. (2) DO NOT BENCH: under that predicate the device is NOT held out and its probes still fire, because the device is not the failing party; a single trouble is raised against the LOOP instead, which is the one party it may make claims about (Law 6). (3) STILL FIRE: the tooth that keeps this honest is that a probe in the affected folder reaches its consumer after detection — a build that detects staleness, records it beautifully, and benches the device anyway leaves the outage exactly where it was.
falsifier.proves_red: RED if: (1) the staleness condition is constructed in a fixture and the device is benched anyway — the outage is unchanged and only the record got prettier; (2) the fix is a better error STRING, so a test that greps the message passes while twenty-two watches stay dark — the message was never the damage, the bench was; (3) the two observed faces are special-cased by symbol name or error text, so the next rename produces a third face and the loop blames the device again; (4) after detection, no probe from the affected folder reaches its consumer; (5) the loop raises the staleness trouble against a DEVICE rather than against itself; (6) the bench-from-live-tickets rule at loop.py:50 is weakened to make this easier — that rule is not the defect and is what made this outage reconstructable at all; (7) the ruled 5s liveness threshold is widened by this build for any reason.
falsifier.horizon: Now, and ahead of the constrain build that was next in Akien's order. The sequencing is not preference: constrain's WATCHME lands in a probes/ folder, and this ticket exists because that folder gets darkened by the loop's own staleness at the next code move. Building a watch into it first would arm a watch born dead — the same shape as the 22 already armed that way.

questions.a: THIS TICKET WAS CAST BEFORE ANY CODE WAS WRITTEN, WHICH IS THE CORRECTION OF THE PROCESS FAILURE RECORDED IN constrain-floor-authors-and-provenance-is-measured. That ticket is parked at TICKETME because its code was built, proven and sealed BEFORE the ticket existed, so the BUILDME entry gate had nothing to judge and I refused to run /chart afterwards to satisfy a check without establishing what it checks for. This one takes the chart route first. The two tickets together are the n=2.

THE OUTAGE WAS LOUD, CORRECTLY RECORDED, AND POINTED AT THE WRONG PARTY — AND BEING POINTED AT THE WRONG PARTY IS WHAT MADE IT QUIET. Fifteen tickets named fifteen devices. The message 'PROBE is Probe, not a Probe' is self-refuting on its face and appeared thirteen times. I read this list at session open TODAY and walked past it, and so did every session before this one. Law 7 got the record right; nothing got the ATTRIBUTION right, and attribution is what decides whether a reader stops.

AN OUTAGE THAT STOPS RECURRING IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM ONE THAT WAS FIXED. Four tickets sat at ~10,286 occurrences with last_seen 23.7h old, which reads as history. The count froze because a benched device is passed to discover() in skip and never re-scanned — so the very mechanism that protects the beat also silences the evidence. The high counts were the devices that failed FAST before benching; the 1x tickets were not the quiet ones.

A RESTART ALONE WOULD NOT HAVE FIXED IT, and this is the trap for whoever meets this next. The bench is defined as 'a live ticket by this name exists' (loop.py:50) and clearing is the recipient's act alone, so a restarted loop keeps every device dark with the imports now perfectly fine and nothing red anywhere. The order that works is: restart, verify through the loop's OWN discover(), then clear — which is the order this session used, with failures==[] confirmed per device before each clear.

THE 2531 ms PER-BEAT TRIGGER COST IS A SEPARATE DEFECT FOUND IN THE SAME ACT AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT FOLDED IN. It could only be measured once the watch layer was actually armed: 22 probes, 2531 ms per beat (build_inspector 705, base 1170 across five, inference_domain 566), beat slowed to ~3.5s against a ruled 5s liveness threshold, so a healthy loop now reads DEAD about a third of the time. The heartbeat had been cheap for 29 hours because it was doing nothing. Folding it in would make one proof carry two unrelated claims; it owes its own ticket.

STILL ABSENT AND OLDER THAN THIS: there is no CLI door for clearing a trouble. This session cleared fifteen through TroubleDevice.clear() in Python, which IS the door and not a bypass, but bin/cmd has no command for it and the session-open banner that surfaces live troubles offers no way to act on them.

THE ENTRY GATE CAUGHT ME WRITING MYSELF AN EXEMPTION, and it was right. This field originally read 'none yet, and deliberately so: this ticket takes the CHART route to BUILDME' — a paragraph reasoning that a berthed chart chain substitutes for an /intent firing. It does not: buildme_rides_the_intent is a SEPARATE check from the chart claim, and the gate refused the crossing naming exactly that. The legal answers were to fire /intent or to record 'none, because <checkable why>', and I had written neither — I had written a rationalisation in the shape of the second. Firing it was not a formality: the model-consult at that gate is what surfaced ground_loop falsifier clause (5), which forbids the heartbeat holding runtime state of its own and therefore RULES OUT capturing per-module load times — the correct comparison for the REWRITTEN evidence. The cheapest gate in the system decided a build detail the six stages above it had left open.

watchme.trigger: each read over the trouble store. TRUE when a live ground-loop-device-* ticket exists whose device folder imports CLEANLY under a fresh discover() — the exact signature of this outage, cheap to evaluate because it is the same discovery the loop already runs. ONE such ticket fires it: this failure mode is silent by construction, so waiting for n is waiting in the dark.
watchme.enough: NEVER CLEARED BY A QUIET PERIOD — a quiet period is precisely what this outage looked like for 29 hours. Cleared only when a live ticket of this shape has been absent ACROSS AT LEAST ONE OBSERVED LOOP RESTART, the event that creates the staleness. Until a restart has been survived, silence is untested rather than evidence.
watchme.carrier: cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/probes/loop_not_stale.py — carrying the live bench tickets, each device's current discover() verdict, the loop's process start time, and the newest mtime in the cairn tree, so a reader separates 'the loop is old' from 'the device is broken' without going back to disk (I-complete-diagnostic-on-first-pass).
watchme.nexus: triage — the finding is 'a device is benched and imports fine', and splitting a stale loop from a genuinely-fixed-but-uncleared defect from a device broken some other way is a routing question, not a hypothesis about mechanism.
watchme.consumer: harbor_master. It deposits and pokes and carries no authority: the back-edge is the owner's act (Law 6). A fire means compare the loop's process start time against the tree's newest mtime FIRST — that one comparison separates the causes, and getting it backwards is how this went unread for 29 hours.

cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/proofs/test_loop_not_stale.py — the WATCH's own proof, sealed netns. It did not exist when the watch was emitted, and that is this voyage's keeper finding.
closed.the_watch_shipped_unproved_and_that_is_t: The probe was discovered, loaded, berthed, and emitted through the emission gate with the suite reading 107/107 green — and its every-beat path raised AttributeError: 'TroubleDevice' object has no attribute 'root' the first time anything CALLED it. It was found while measuring the probe's per-beat cost for the exit gate, not by any test. A second defect sat in the same function: the cheap half globbed FILENAMES for the bench prefix, and a file keeps its name after it is cleared, so it counted dead tickets as benches and disagreed with the expensive half exactly when a bench had just been lifted — the state that follows someone acting on this probe's own advice. Both are fixed by asking the store's own live() door. THE SHAPE IS THE TICKET'S OWN, ONE LEVEL UP: a watch that cannot run is a watch that is off, and this whole voyage is about a watch layer being switched off without anyone seeing. The emission gate proves a probe is berthed and armed; nothing proved it could RUN. Armed by hand is not wired, and the diagnostic is to call it.
closed.the_falsifier_answered_clause_by_clause: None of the seven RED clauses fired. (1) The condition was not constructed in a fixture and waved at — criterion 9 ran against the live daemon, and the first two attempts produced NO condition at all: moving probe.py, then move plus mtime bump, changed nothing, because sys.modules caches the dotted name and a re-exec'd probe rebinds the SAME class object. That diagnosis is part of the evidence, not a detour. (3) Neither face is special-cased by symbol name or error text; the predicate is a relation between a process start time and file mtimes, so a third face falls out of it too. (4) A probe from the affected folder reaches its consumer after detection — proved, not asserted. (5) The trouble is raised against the LOOP. (6) The bench-from-live-tickets rule at loop.py:50 is untouched. (7) The ruled 5s liveness threshold is untouched, which was Akien's one named bound.
reds_dispositioned_not_explained: probescan reds 23 of 23. MEASURED, not argued: can_receive opens with DiscoveredShim(device_id) for every id, and DiscoveredShim._start_device raises NotImplementedError by design — so the column is a constant and the instrument is structurally incapable of ever returning 3-resolved. Proven by the librarian, which probescan calls unable to receive while LibrarianShim returns a device with a callable receive. 22 of the 23 predate this build and it red 18 of 18 the day it was born. Ticketed at probescan-resolves-the-real-shim-not-a-discovered-one, with the bound that the fix may NOT be to make DiscoveredShim return something.
The AttributeError above — fixed in this voyage, not filed.

chart_leg_findings: DECOMPOSE, and it is the one that cost the voyage its keeper defect. The split named a piece for the probe and NO piece for the probe's proof. So the watch was built, armed, emitted through the emission gate, and shipped raising AttributeError on its every-beat path — and no stage of the chain was ever going to ask for a tooth on it, because the tooth was not in the split. The emission gate proves berthed-and-armed; the split is where 'and it runs' had to be a piece, and was not.

TRIAGE. The order covered the split and the split was complete under its own rules, so nothing was dropped — and the exit gate still handed the voyage a body of unranked work: disposing probescan's 23/23 red took a measurable share of the 215 and appears in no rank. The standing reds a crossing will meet are knowable at triage time (probescan red 18/18 the day it was born) and the chain has no field that asks.

SURVEY. The refs never listed the crossing machinery the close runs on — TesterDevice.run_proof, persist_validation, clearance.clear, boat_owner_of — so each was opened cold at the close, and one of them cost a full refusal to learn: boat_id is the TICKET id, not the device id. That is arguable as out-of-bounds (survey scoped the build, not the close), and it is named rather than filed because the same four calls end every code-seam voyage and no survey has ever listed them.
for_akien: The per-beat trigger cost is 2531 ms and this build measured it rather than estimating it. This probe's own share is a median 2.1 ms (n=15, max 2.4) for the cheap half and 38 ms for the expensive half, which only runs when a bench actually stands. The 2531 ms belongs to the beat, not to this ticket, and is owed its own ticket.

Done here is THE LOOP NO LONGER BLAMES A DEVICE FOR ITS OWN AGE, not THE WATCH LAYER IS HEALTHY. The watch that answers the second question is now armed and, for the first time, proved to run. Its efficacy answer comes later, from the probe, against this ticket's falsifier.

dependencies: MEASURED, not assumed: the trouble lane already has both doors (raise_trouble / clear with required what_changed) and an append-only occurrence history, and it recorded this entire outage faithfully — it is the only reason the timeline could be reconstructed at all. Nothing in the lane needs changing.

ProbeCache's mtime keying is CORRECT and out of scope: it invalidates the probe FILE properly. What it does not do — invalidate the dependency closure — is the gap, and the fix is a predicate on the failure path rather than a wider cache.
discovery.load_module already execs each probe off its path under a synthetic name, which is what makes the fresh binding (and therefore the identity mismatch) happen; it is correct and stays.
read_liveness and its ruled 5s threshold are read-only here.

filed_edges: THE SESSION-OPEN BANNER SURFACES LIVE TROUBLES AND OFFERS NO WAY TO ACT ON THEM, and no bin/cmd command clears one. Fifteen stale troubles survived many sessions of being displayed. A surface that shows a red with no door beside it trains its reader to scroll past — which is measurably what happened.

NOTHING RESTARTS THE GROUND LOOP. It runs as a bare `python3 -m cairn.devices.ground_loop` from the repo root with no systemd unit, no launcher, and no supervision; the 29-hour-old process was the one started by hand. A heartbeat whose own lifecycle is unmanaged will drift from the code again, and this ticket only makes that drift LEGIBLE rather than impossible.

A PROBE'S TRIGGER HAS NO COST BUDGET AND NOTHING MEASURES ONE. Individual triggers here run 700ms and no gate anywhere reds a probe for being expensive; the 2531 ms total was invisible until the layer was armed.
